queries.text: The original spells the English term "batttered man syndrome" (typo); corrected to "battered man syndrome," as the author writes it in 06-0019.

The original note reads "Em português: 'síndrome do homem maltratado'" ("In Portuguese: 'syndrome of the mistreated man'"), glossing the English term for Brazilian readers. Rendered as a gloss in English so no Portuguese remains; alternative: drop the "In Portuguese" framing as done, or have a TN explain that the term was in English in the original.
